'''Richard Mead Goody''' (19 June 1921 – 3 August 2023) was a British-American atmospheric physicist and professor of planetary physics at [[Harvard University]].<ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=lldYAAAAMAAJ&q=%22Goody,+richard+mead%22+1921 American Men & Women of Science - Google Books<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref><ref>[http://www.seas.harvard.edu/directory/goody Richard Goody], [[Harvard School of Engineering and Applied Sciences]]</ref> He was inducted into the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 1970.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/richard-m-goody-uafekz/ | title=Richard M. Goody | work=NAS Website | access-date=9 May 2014}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
A native of [[Hertfordshire]], Goody attended [[Cambridge University]], from which he received a bachelor's degree in physics in 1942. He then worked at the [[Aeroplane and Armament Experimental Establishment]] until October 1946, when he returned to Cambridge to receive his PhD, doing so in 1949.<ref name=Goody/> While there, he was instructed to build an [[infrared spectrometer]] for use in an airplane to measure stratospheric dryness.<ref name=Goody/> He also made important discoveries into the structure of the [[stratosphere]] during this time, which led him to study [[radiative transfer]] in planetary atmospheres.<ref name=bowie/> 

Related to this work, the best known and widely used model of absorption bands in atmospheric opacity is due to the work of Goody in 1952, and the model was initially known as the Goody random model. It was later discovered that [[Harris Mayer]]'s work under the supervision of [[Edward Teller]] at [[Los Alamos National Laboratory]] published in 1947 had made similar calculations and many sources now call the model the Mayer-Goody model or the Mayer-Goody statistical model.<ref>Timofeyev, Yu M., and Aleksander Vladimirovich Vasilʹev. Theoretical fundamentals of atmospheric optics. Cambridge Int Science Publishing, 2008. pg. 294</ref>

==Scientific career==
Goody was appointed the [[Abbott Lawrence Rotch]] Professor of Dynamic Meteorology and director of the [[Blue Hill Observatory]] at Harvard in 1958<ref name=bowie/> and elected into the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] the following year.<ref name=HDC>[http://www.cfa.harvard.edu/hitran/Download/Proceedings-98.pdf Hitran Database Conference], p. 8</ref> He became a US citizen in 1965.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.irc-iamas.org/awards/2004_rgoody.php | title=IRC Awards 2004 - Gold Medal | work=International Radiation Commission | date=2004 | accessdate=9 May 2014}}</ref> His 1964 book ''Atmospheric Radiation'' has been described as "classic".<ref name=bowie/> He served as the director of the Blue Hill Observatory until 1970,<ref>[http://www.history.nasa.gov/biose-j.html Biographies of Aerospace Officials and Policymakers, E-J]</ref> and the chair of the Space Studies Board of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] from 1974 to 1976.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://sites.nationalacademies.org/ssb/ssb_052281 | title=Board Members and Staff | publisher=National Academy of Science | accessdate=10 May 2014}}</ref> 

In 1970, Goody was the co-chair of a National Academy of Sciences study of [[Venus]] entitled "Venus: Strategy for Exploration",<ref>{{cite book | title=Venus Strategy for Exploration | publisher=National Academy of Sciences | year=1970 | pages=R4}}</ref> and he was partly responsible for launching the [[Pioneer Venus project]], which launched probes to Venus in 1978.<ref name=Goody/> He underwent compulsory retirement from Harvard in 1991.<ref name=Goody/> Goody was elected to the [[American Philosophical Society]] in 1997.<ref>{{Cite web|title=APS Member History|url=https://search.amphilsoc.org/memhist/search?creator=Richard+M.+Goody&title=&subject=&subdiv=&mem=&year=&year-max=&dead=&keyword=&smode=advanced|access-date=2021-12-10|website=search.amphilsoc.org}}</ref>

==Death==
Goody died on 3 August 2023, at the age of 102.<ref>[https://www.peacefulalternatives.com/obituary/richard-goody Richard Mead Goody obituary], peacefulalternatives.com. Accessed November 12, 2023.</ref>
